claims.claim: Very good condition, just buy and use.
claims.evidence: The witness report only covers the exterior appearance; functionality was not tested.
The witness identified the brand 'Ideal' but did not report seeing a 'Made in Japan' stamp or plate.
Motor performance and sound cannot be determined from still photos.

claims.claim: All accessories and the original manual included.
claims.evidence: The witness specifically noted that accessories and the manual were not shown.

claims.claim: Never serviced because nothing ever went wrong.
claims.evidence: Service history is an internal matter that cannot be confirmed through visual inspection.

risks.risk: The motor may be seized or burnt out.
risks.proof: A video clip of the machine running and the needle moving via the foot pedal.

risks.risk: Voltage incompatibility (Japanese domestic machines are often 110V, while Nigeria is 220V).
risks.proof: A clear photo of the electrical rating plate on the motor or back of the machine.
risks.if_unproven: As requiring an external transformer or motor replacement.

risks.risk: Internal timing issues or cracked gears (common in vintage machines).
risks.proof: A video showing the machine successfully picking up the bobbin thread and completing a stitch.
risks.if_unproven: As requiring professional mechanical timing service.

proof_requests: A photo of the model number plate (usually on the front, side, or base).
A photo of the electrical specification plate showing voltage (V) and frequency (Hz).
A video of the machine sewing through a piece of fabric.
Photos of the included accessories and manual.
response.reason: The specific model number is missing, and for a sewing machine, functional proof and voltage compatibility are essential to establish even a base value.
